name: Luxury workwear

lead: Luxury workwear takes garments built for manual trades, like canvas jackets, heavy denim, work boots and boiler suits, and wears them in higher-quality fabrics and cuts. The appearance payoff is a rugged but polished silhouette.
Workwear has a long fashion history, from 1980s street subcultures to 21st-century denim and chambray trends, and brands such as Carhartt have crossed into streetwear and designer collaborations.

paras: People pair a work jacket, raw denim or chinos and sturdy boots, often in muted tones, choosing fit and fabric quality over logos.
Mainly cost and fit: heavy fabrics can look boxy if sized poorly.

chain: Utility garments in better fabric and fit
angle.text: Wearers use work jackets, denim and boots as a base for an outfit that reads as deliberate and understated.

lead: Luxury workwear refers to premium takes on utility clothing. Wikipedia's history of workwear traces trade clothing from Victorian donkey jackets and railroad overalls to its adoption as street attire in the 1980s and, in the 21st century, its influence on streetwear and hipster style, including denim jackets, chambray shirts, raw denim and work boots.[1]

Carhartt, founded in Detroit in 1889 to make labourers' clothing, expanded into fashion via hip-hop in the 1990s, the 1994 Carhartt WIP streetwear line, and collaborations with A.P.C., Comme des Garcons and other labels.[2]
For appearance, workwear pieces give structure to shoulders and a masculine, utilitarian silhouette.

paras: Workwear signalled occupation in Victorian Britain, and American and Asian trade clothing also developed distinct forms.[1]
Street subcultures adopted work boots and donkey jackets in the 1980s; later denim and boots shaped hipster style.[1] Carhartt WIP and its designer collaborations are one example of the crossover.[2]
